==English==

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before|*ḱyesdʰ-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|proces}}, from {{der|en|fro|procés||journey}}, from {{der|en|la|prōcessus||course, progression}}, nominalization of {{m|la|prōcēdō||proceed, advance}}.

====Pronunciation====
* {{enPR|prōʹsĕs|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹəʊ.sɛs/}}
** {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-process.wav|a=UK}}
* {{enPR|prŏʹsĕs|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑ.sɛs/|/-əs/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-process.ogg|a=US}}
* {{enPR|prōʹsĕs|a=Canada,rarely US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹoʊ.sɛs/|/-əs/}} (noun only, the verb is pronounced as in the US)
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹəʉˌses/|[ˈpɹɐʉˌses]|a=AU}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɐʉˌses/|a=NZ}}
* {{hyph|en|pro|cess}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q10843872}}A [[series]] of [[event]]s leading to a [[result]] or [[product]].
#: {{ux|en|This [[product]] of last month's quality standards committee is quite good, even though the '''process''' was flawed.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=September 27, 2011|author=Alistair Magowan|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/14982446.stm Bayern Munich 2-0 Man City]
|passage=But they came up against an impressive force in Bayern, who extended their run to 10 wins on the trot, having scored 28 goals in the '''process''' and conceding none.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=68
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21579860-g8-pledges-tackle-three-ts-t-time T time]
|passage=Yet in “Through a Latte, Darkly”, a new study of how Starbucks has largely avoided paying tax in Britain, Edward Kleinbard {{...}} shows that current tax rules make it easy for all sorts of firms to generate what he calls “stateless income”: {{...}} In Starbucks’s case, the firm has in effect turned the '''process''' of making an expensive cup of coffee into intellectual property.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q2281940}} {{lb|en|manufacturing}} The [[set]] of [[procedure]]s used in the manufacture of a [[product]], especially in the [[food]] and [[chemical]] industries.
# A path or succession of states through which a [[system]] passes.
# {{lb|en|biology}} Successive physiological responses to keep or restore health.
# {{lb|en|legal}} Documents issued by a court in the course of a lawsuit or action at law, such as a [[summons]], [[mandate]], or [[writ]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1711|author=John Spotiswood|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iyVWAAAAYAAJ|title=The Form of Process|section=39
|passage=But if either at ''Calling'' by the Clerk, after the ''Session Bell'', or before the Ordinary by the ''Roll'', an ''Advocat'' compears, and craves to be ''Marked'' for the ''Defender'', and to see the '''''Process'''''; The ''Clerk'' in the first ''Case'', and the ''Judge'' in the second, will allow him to see it}}
# {{lb|en|anatomy}} An outgrowth of [[tissue]] arising above a surface, such as might form part of a [[joint]] or the attachment point for a [[muscle]].
# {{senseid|en|Q205663}}{{lb|en|computing}} An [[executable]] [[task]] or [[program]].
# The centre mark that players aim at in the game of [[squails]].

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To perform a particular process on a thing.
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=Spin Off|year=2026|volume=L|number=1|page=16|title=Yagaa: Reviving Sericulture in Southern Mexico|author=Elise Young
|text='''Processing''' the harvested cocoons begins with grading and then boiling them in soapy water to soften the sericin that binds the fibers together.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To retrieve, store, classify, manipulate, transmit etc. (data, signals, etc.), especially using computer techniques.
#: {{ux|en|We have '''processed''' the data using our proven techniques, and have come to the following conclusions.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Lighting and the Dramatic Portrait|publisher=Amphoto Books|author=w:Michael Grecco|year=2006|ISBN=9780817442279|page=92
|passage=If you '''process''' you own digital files, it's as time consuming, or maybe even more time consuming, than it is to '''process''' and print your own film.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Elisabeth Buchwald and Ramishah Maruf|title=A massive tariff on millions of Americans’ purchases just went into effect — cue the chaos|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/02/economy/de-minimis-packages-tariff|date=2025-05-02|passage=CBP told CNN it currently '''processes''' “nearly 4 million duty-free de minimis shipments a day.”|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260514181120/https://www.cnn.com/2025/05/02/economy/de-minimis-packages-tariff|archivedate=14 May 2026}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To think about a piece of information, or a concept, in order to [[assimilate]] it, and perhaps [[accept]] it in a modified state.
#: {{ux|en|I didn't know she had a criminal record. That will take me a while to '''process'''.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|photography|film}} To [[develop]] photographic film.
# {{lb|en|transitive|legal}} To take legal proceedings against.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1845|title=Report from Her Majesty's Commissioners of inquiry into the state of the law and practice in respect to the occupation of land in Ireland
|passage=When I saw that he would not let me alone, I '''processed''' him for £12. My mother was with his brother John, and he allowed her six guineas for clothes; and if she did not want the money, he would allow it to me in the rent, and I made him pay that when he would not leave me alone.}}
